title: Module Import Flow
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Three file cards (config.py, motors.py, main.py) linked by import arrows. Changing RIGHT_FORWARD_PIN in config.py updates every file that imports config, while a hard-coded version leaves five stale numbers and a disconnected motor wire.

educational.topic: Modules, import, and the config.py pattern
learningObjectives: Explain how import links config.py, motors.py, and main.py.
Describe the order in which modules load when main.py runs, including that a module loads only once.
Predict which files change behavior when one value in config.py changes.
Compare the number of edits needed with the config.py pattern and with hard-coded pin numbers.
standards: CSTA 3A-AP-17: Decompose problems into smaller components through systematic analysis, using constructs such as procedures, modules, and/or objects

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Cause-and-effect demonstration with a contrasting counter-example (hard-coded pins)
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Students run main.py to see the import order step by step, change the pin in config.py to see it propagate, and toggle hard-coded pins to see what breaks.
keyQuestions: Why does config.py load only once when two files import it?
Which lines change when you edit RIGHT_FORWARD_PIN in config.py?
What goes wrong when the pin number is typed by hand in five places?
commonMisconceptions: Each file needs its own copy of the pin numbers.
Changing config.py also changes numbers typed directly into other files.
A module that is imported twice runs twice.
import copies the code into the file instead of linking to the module.
assessmentOpportunities: Write down the console order after Run main.py and explain it.
Challenge: count the lines to edit with and without config.py when a wire moves to pin 13.
Exit ticket: explain the risk of editing a pin in motors.py instead of config.py.
